title: Guiding lights to the stars
caption: The ESO 3.6-metre telescope under the Large Magellanic Cloud, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The ESO 3.6-metre telescope sits on the summit of La Silla, 2400 m above sea level in the Atacama Desert. At the top of the picture shines the Large Magellanic Cloud, a dwarf galaxy that orbits our own Milky Way.

The site offers ideal conditions for watching the sky. The desert air is dry and clouds are rare, and being far from cities keeps the sky dark. A faint green airglow near the horizon comes naturally from molecules high in Earth's atmosphere. Even the warm, dim lights along the access road at the bottom of the frame are meant to keep light pollution low.
This telescope is home to HARPS, the High Accuracy Radial velocity Planet Searcher, a highly productive planet-hunting instrument.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the faint green airglow and the Large Magellanic Cloud appear stronger than they would to an observer.

explore: In the Mapuche culture, the Large Magellanic Cloud has several names: lafken, labken or künchalabken, meaning lagoon, and rünanko, meaning water well. It is one of the Milky Way's neighbouring galaxies and appears here at the top of the frame.
alt: A telescope on a mountain summit at night with a faint green glow on the horizon, dim road lights at the bottom and a galaxy at the top.
